lines.line: Hmm?
Is there anything I can help you with?
Nah. I don't think so.
Don't bother me, peasant. I've had a long journey and paid too much coin on these gifts to be late to Vittoria's wedding.
Enjoy the wedding.
Indeed. If we ever get there.
Loyal Nords are always welcome here. Anyone else better watch their step.
If I were you, I'd keep away from the barrow on the east side of town... it's haunted.
I'd like to rent a room. (10 gold)
Sure thing. It's yours for a day.
If there are five hundred steps to each marker then maybe...Argh! This is pointless. Dar'Rakki can not rely on shortcuts!
Any thoughts on the townsfolk?
This is a good place to hide one's identity, no? Ivarstead attracts those who cling to lofty ideals. They never suspect our faces are two.
You see those warriors from Hammerfell? They've got curved swords. Curved. Swords.
What do you play?
I play the lute. If you'd like to hear something, it only costs five gold.
This has to be the worst place in Skyrim to run a mill. How am I supposed to do anything with all those bears running around?
What's making you so angry?
My business is falling apart, my apprentice never listens to me and now there's talk of dragons.
If I hadn't sunk every bit of gold I had into my mill, I would have picked up and left Ivarstead long ago.
You want a drink?
What's on the menu?
Depends. Are you thirsty, hungry, both?
Anything you can tell me about High Hrothgar?
I've always fancied a journey up the 7,000 Steps to the monastery.
Anything to break the boredom of living in this town. I envy you.
Need something?
All right, hand over your valuables, or I'll gut you like a fish.
Walk away. Right now. (Intimidate)
Nice try, but you don't scare me.
I'm not going to ask again.
I'd rather die!
Then I guess that's your last request, fool!
Hmph.
What have you got for sale?
Take a look.
Yes?
And what might you need? Hmm?
Is there anything I can help you with?
Nah. I don't think so.
Looking for my husband Nazeem? Check the Jarl's backside. That's usually where he stuffs himself these days.
Is there anything I can help you with?
Maybe you can help me.
What do you need?
Of course.
Of course.
Of course.
It's all in this note.
Never been to Whiterun before? The Jarl's palace is something to see. Big old dragon skull hanging on the wall. Impressive.
What do you know about Whiterun?
Well, I know the Companions make their home here. Their mead hall, Jorrvaskr, is the oldest building in the city.
Oh, and there's a nasty feud between two families called the Gray-Manes and the Battle-Borns. You'll want to be careful there.
The rest you can find out by asking the townsfolk. I'd start with the barkeep at the Bannered Mare, or the castle Steward.
Think you can go blade to blade with me? You'd be dead in six seconds.
You think you can take me on?
And why not? I could beat anyone in this city, bare-handed.
A hundred gold says I knock your hide to the ground.
I've got better things to do.
Pfft. Snowback.
You must really love to fight.
The heat of the battle is the fire that forges the strongest blades. It's an old Nord proverb.
That, and a true Nord never misses a chance to test her worth.
Sounds like you've got a grudge.
You been talking to those Companions?
"Too hot-headed," they cried. Weak, pathetic cowards, the lot of them!
Why'd the Companions reject you?
It wasn't my fault! I told them over and over that it was an accident!
They wanted me to prove my worth, so they threw me up against a young whelp of a lad, hardly old enough to grow his first chin hairs.
I guess they thought a woman wasn't strong enough to hurt him. I didn't mean for him to die! Why would I want that? I just... I just lost control.
Want to hear a little Nord wisdom? You don't really know a woman 'til you've had a strong drink and a fistfight with her.
You think you can take me on?
And why not? I could beat anyone in this city, bare-handed.
A hundred gold says I knock your hide to the ground.
You're on. (Brawl - 100 gold)
Just fists. No weapons, no magic... no crying. Let's go!
Now that's what I call a punch. You got me.
I think I've earned that 100 gold.
You're no liar. Best fight I've had in years. There you are.
If you ever need another blade at your side, just ask. Wouldn't mind seeing how you handle a few trolls.
Ain't every day we get visitors in Riverwood.
Need any help around the forge?
Yes, actually. How about you smith me an iron dagger? Here's everything you need to make one. Go ahead.
Whatever you need. By Ysmir, if it's simple and strong, I can forge it.
Here's an iron dagger.
Not bad, but it's a little dull. How about you sharpen it up? Just need a bit of metal and the grindstone over there.
I don't know what you overheard, but the Riverwood Trader is still open. Feel free to shop.
What happened here?
Uh yeah, we did have a bit of a... a break-in. But we still have plenty to sell. Robbers were only after one thing.
An ornament, solid gold. In the shape of a dragon's claw.
I could help you get the claw back.
You could? I've got some coin coming in from my last shipment. It's yours if you bring my claw back.
Mara bless you for agreeing to help us.
How much farther do I have to walk?
Well, it's a winding road up the mountain just ahead. You'll know you're in the right place once you spot the old watchtower.
Once you get to the tower, head north. Bleak Falls Barrow should be just around the corner further up.
Faendal thinks he can woo Camilla Valerius away from me. She's already mine, I keep telling him.
You and Faendal both like the same girl?
Camilla Valerius knows I'm the best man in Riverwood. That elf is kidding himself if he thinks she would choose him over me.
I've seen him sneaking over to the Riverwood Trader to speak with her when I'm not around. He's wasting his time.
Yes. Two people spending time together never blossoms into courtship.
Is that sarcasm? I've heard better wisecracks from Orgnar.
Still, you have a point. Camilla letting Faendal visit her isn't a good thing for me.
Here, let me give you a particularly venomous letter. Say it's from Faendal. That should get Camilla to stop inviting the elf over.
Sure, why not?  This ought to be amusing.
That letter ought to convince Camilla to never speak to Faendal ever again.
Mara bless you for agreeing to help us.
Sven wanted to trick you into believing this letter was from Faendal.
What are you talking about? What's in the letter?
Oh my. He... he wanted me to think Faendal wrote this?
Thank you for telling me the truth. Could you talk to Faendal, as well?  I'm sure he'll want to thank you for standing up for him.
Riverwood's agreeable enough, I suppose. For a Nord village.
I don't think Camilla will be spending any more time with Sven.
I appreciate your help. Please, take this. Some gold I've saved up from working at the mill.
They say the College has been snooping around Saarthal. Mages in a burial crypt. No good can come of that...
What can you tell me about Riverwood?
It's my mill. Some folks thinks it's my town, too, but it ain't. The Jarl in Whiterun owns the land and the town. I just pay the taxes.
Greetings stranger, the name's Hjoromir, and I'm at your service.
Let me know if there's anything I can help you with.  Perhaps you need your boots shined, or your tunic washed, or need a letter delivered?
No, no, and maybe.  Do you have a quill?
Oh right, I knew I forgot something.  Is it a long missive?  Perhaps I can memorize it.
Dear dragon, I'm coming back for you.  Paladin Regina, dictated but not signed.
Okay, Dear Dragon, I'm going...or was it coming?  Can you repeat that?
Confound it boy, are you daft?  No one is this slow.
Yes, if that's what you need.  I can be your personal jester, and you can mock me for your amusement.
But I can be much more than that.  I can polish your boots, gather your kindling, and carry your quiver, handing you arrows as you shoot them.
I'll consider it.
R-really?  I'll do everything you ask, just say the word!
Do you have a job in town?
If you're asking if I specialize in something, I'd say I do just about everything.  For instance, I used to help Sven chop lumber.
That is, until the day he almost lost his hand at the sawmill.  Wasn't my fault, he ran into me.  But he hasn't asked for my help since.
Same with Delphine. She says I broke too many dishes. I broke maybe three at the most.
So I take it she treats you harshly.
Yeah, that woman seems sweet on the outside, but beware, she has a real mean streak too.
Gerdur though, she'll vouch for me. And the blacksmith fellow, I forget his name.  He taught me how to strip leather down.
I'm guessing he would've hired me as his apprentice, but I think he knew I was destined for more.
I'm sensing a pattern with your previous employers.
I know what you're getting at.  I hear the whispers.  But the only pattern I see is one of versatility.
I mean I'm no fool.  Yes, I can be clumsy.  And Mara knows I'm not the best cook.
But that's only because I'm not really concentrating on what I'm doing.  And why should I?
It's not as if the lumber chopping and dish washing is a mentally exhausting skill.
I figure I can do that stuff while I fill my head with greater pursuits.
I take it you are referring to the pursuit of knowledge.
You need to be more cognizant of the times, traveler.  And the place.  Skyrim cares naught for knowledge.
What good is becoming a scholar?  Only a handful of people will understand the things you say and they'll still disagree on the meaning.
In Skyrim, people understand only one thing.  The cry of battle.  Blood and steel.  And songs to immortalize the heroes and the dead.
That's what will get you the adulation of your peers.  Not reading some dusty old book.
Adventuring is no child's game, boy.
Ha, you sound like my father.  Where were you eighteen years ago on the 14th of Frostfall?
I'll tell you what I told him.  I don't plan to go out into the wilderness unprepared.  I've been in countless fights already.
In fact, I'm fighting right now, even as we speak.
You're fairly young for someone living out on his own.
I'm of age, and a man grown.  I can grow whiskers on my cheeks just like any old Nord.
People treat me differently because of my station, but they still respect me as a man.  Which is more than I can say for my father.
The last time I saw the old toad all he did was bark orders and gripe.  He complained my pheasant roast was overcooked.
He nearly slapped me when I poured his beer and left a less than frothy head, and then he berated me the entire time I cleared the table.
Sounds like a volatile household.
Yeah, but at least when he's eating he keeps his mouth shut.  The worst part is afterward, when he starts spouting racist nonsense.
Elves poisoning our food. Elves stealing our children. And don't tell him there's a difference between the Elven races, let alone Altmer and Thalmor.
They're all Thalmor maggots to him. Listening to the old man makes me ashamed to call myself a Nord.
What about your mother?
Ah, my mother is a kind woman.  She always compliments me on my meals, and tells me how proud she is to have me for a son.
That's it's own dilemma.  When even I can tell my potage has no flavor, it's tough to appreciate the kindness of her words.
While lies of deceit are born as spiders and die as flies, white lies can wilt like a rose and leave nothing but thorns.
Any siblings?
Just one. A sister. A real snobby bitch, and obsessed with gold. Saving it to be precise.  Which would be fine, if she had a sense of humor about it.
Whenever we went to the market in Whiterun, she'd always harass the vendors until they gave her a discount just to make her leave.
Poor Carlotta. Here she was trying everything in her power to feed her children, and my sister shakes her down for every last septim.
When we left, I told my sister, if there was one thing she didn't need any amulet or potion for, it was to become a master of cheapcraft.
That pretty much severed whatever relationship we had.  My sister holds a grudge as tight as she holds her coin purse.
That's enough about your family.
And I've had enough of talking about them, as it were.  At least, to anyone who isn't a patron.
You in need of a companion, friend?  Well, then you're in luck.
I reckon I've killed more men then there are minutes in a day.
You've killed more than 1,440 men?
That few, huh?  At this rate, I guess I better change it to "seconds" then. (Laughs)  But who's counting.
What brought you to Skyrim?
The horkers, my friend, the horkers!  I can't get enough of a good bowl of horker stew.  Fresh garlic, tomatoes, a sprinkle of lavender...
It sounds delicious except for the horker part.
You jest, but there's nothing like good horker stew.  It ain't like the loaf, which is a bit chewy and marinated in that ocean flavor.
But you put that in a stew, toss in a little garlic, and all that ocean brine melts into pure flavor.
You're in the wrong place. Riverwood isn't exactly the horker capital of Skyrim.
That isn't it. You see, I've tried stews of all different flavors from all over Tamriel.
I've tried your venisons and your steaks.  I've tried your bug meat, your hoarver pies and chaurus nuggets.
Some Wood Elf charlatan even tried to sell me what he called a wyvern steak, but it tasted like a mountain goat.
I've tried every meat from the Summerset Isle to the shores of Solstheim, and ain't nothing compare to a fresh pot of horker stew.
But you know what I haven't tried?  I haven't tried a dragon.  And call me crazy, but I think I saw one fly this way not long ago.
There was a dragon at Helgen.  You probably saw that one.
You don't say.  Sounds like Embry owes me a drink.  Said I was more likely to see a horker with wings.
(Laughs) I reckon that would be too good to be true.
Where did you learn to fight?
I got my start as a pit dog in the Imperial City Arena.  Worked my way up to Gladiator before I got bored and quit.
They say the best techniques are left by the survivors.  With me gone, I guess everyone will have something to offer.
Gladiator, huh? Impressive.
I know, and I would've been Grand Champion too, if not for the burden.
Oh, I know what you're thinking.  Fair maidens in my bed, and good stew in my belly.  Some burden.  Well, that ain't what I'm talking about.
Why did you leave the arena?
Well friend, it all comes down to who your opponent is.  I'm square with killing men, but with a Grand Champion, ain't no more men to fight.
So they bring in beasts.  Minotaurs and things.  Don't like it one bit.  If a man chooses to enter the arena, it's what you call his prerogative.
A beast ain't got no say in the matter.  I kill horkers for food, and bears for hides.  I don't kill no animal for sport.
Why did you become an arena fighter?
Why not? You need to get out more, friend. The Arena is the most celebrated spectacle in all of Tamriel.
To fight and die in the Arena is a great honor. To fight and live, well, do that and you carve your name amongst the Gods.
The appetite for bloodsport could not have been high after the war.
You're mistaken.  It couldn't have been higher.  The people were hungry, not for blood, but for entertainment.
The Arena, friend, was a welcome diversion from the throes of war.  Because there's no death in the Arena.  Not to them.
If you're a spectator, ain't nothing that happens in that pit real.  It's all a game.
What makes the Arena so popular?
'Cause it's fair.  It's about the only place you can truly measure a man's worth.
If I asked the folks here who has the best mead in Skyrim, one person might say Black-Briar mead. Another might vouch for Honningbrew.
If I asked for the best alchemist, bard, or scribe, or which inn was warmest, and which wench the sweetest, there'd be many replies, but no answer.
Ah, but if I asked you who was the strongest, who could best any man in the pit, there'd be no debate.  You'd know by who was left standing.
Only in the Arena can a man be judged by his own merits.
Describe the Arena experience.
The words won't do it justice, not mine, anyway.  But you can imagine, can't you?  That moment when you stand behind the gate, in a cold sweat.
The air's so thick you can taste the blood.  The crowd is buzzing.  The flies are buzzing.  Then they wheel up the iron.
You hear this roar.  So loud it rumbles in your chest.  You don't know who they cheer for.  What they cheer for.  Victory, glory, or death.
But that's the beauty of the Arena, ain't it.  Nothing's ever written, nothing's ever known.
The Grand Champion can win a hundred matches and name a skeever as his next opponent, and the audience will still hold their breath.
Unlike the stories, it's always a surprise when the hero wins.  'Cause in the Arena, the hero's allowed to fail.
I'm more interested in the gambling aspect.
Can't tell you much about that.  I mean, I heard the whispers.
Sometimes you see good fighters lose to pit dogs.  Next day, they show up with swords so enchanted they crapped mages when you swung 'em.
There was one Khajiit fighter the others called "Jingle."  Said every night he went home, win or lose, his pockets jingled with gold.
But ain't no one ever approached me.  They knew where I stood. I grew up watching the fights. I learned enough then to know glory was the best coin.
That's all the questions I have about the Arena.
You ought to travel to Cyrodiil sometime, friend, and test your valor.
What's on your mind?
Have you ever heard of a clannfear? Lizard beasts from Oblivion. Taste like chicken, or so I've been told.
Hmm?
Here. Have a drink on me.
Got any ale or mead?
What do you want?
Can I help you?
We got rooms and food. Drink too. I cook. Ain't much else to tell.
I heard of a new gang of bandits hiding at Sewers of Whiterun...
Here. Take a look at this. Some of the Jarl's men came by and left this bounty letter.
Any news or rumors floating about?
Here. Take a look at this.
Heard any rumors lately?
Have you seen that Shrine of Azura? They say the Dark Elves built it after they fled from Morrowind. Sight to see.
Heard any rumors lately?
Nobody trusts those mages, way up north in their College. Gods only know what they do up there.
Heard any rumors lately?
We've got something of a love triangle here in Riverwood. Faendal and Sven, both vying for Camilla's affections.
Heard any rumors lately?
They say a dragon attacked Helgen. Sounds like hogwash to me.
You're that visitor, been pokin' around.
Heard any rumors lately?
Word is Ulfric Stormcloak escaped from the Imperials. War's only going to get worse, now.
Heard any rumors lately?
They say a dragon attacked Helgen. Sounds like hogwash to me.
I'd like to rent a room. (10 gold)
Sure thing. It's yours for a day.
You're that visitor, been pokin' around.
